problem: Prior instruction-following navigation models often rely on symbolic or pre-processed inputs, so they do not learn from raw visual input and natural text together and do not transfer to real visual data.
motivation: A virtual robot should learn to follow novel navigational instructions from instruction-perception examples alone. An architecture that consumes raw pixels could also work on real images, not only on the synthetic environment it was trained in.
key_idea: A visually grounded deep network maps raw visual input and natural-language instructions to navigation actions, is trained on data from a synthetic environment, and has an architecture that also accepts real visual data.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablations or analysis could be read. The abstract claims that learning end to end from instruction-perception pairs gives results on par with earlier methods, and that the architecture is compatible with real visual data.
method: Visually grounded model: a deep network that processes raw visual observations and natural text instructions jointly to produce navigation actions.
Training data: instruction-perception examples collected in a synthetic environment.
Real-data compatibility: the architecture is designed so it can also take real visual input (details not given in the abstract).

setting.backbone: deep visually grounded neural network (details not given in abstract)
setting.training_data: instruction-perception examples collected in a synthetic environment (scale not stated)
setting.observation: raw visual input (RGB) plus natural language instruction

results: The abstract says the results are on par with previously proposed methods. It gives no numbers and names no baselines.
